reason: This board has no newly measured candidate. Rank the NEON transpose first as a targeted alternative for the previously measured TB path, while treating its poor whole-call results only as a reason for caution, not proof that transpose caused them. Four-step unrolling is a distinct extension, but may increase code and register pressure; padding to 288 bytes has no established cache benefit and follows a rejected 272-byte layout. Half-band packing adds repacking to a traversal with no prior promotion. The K-pair proposal may alias the measured two-step unroll unless its actual instruction schedule differs. Fused transpose repeats A-tile work across column panels. TA adds both timed conversion and generated A packing while retaining B packing. These are priority judgments from the supplied evidence, not predictions of measured gains.
